name: Sonnet concentrated AI/technology
strategy: Concentrated long book in AI infrastructure leaders (compute, networking, memory) with leveraged semis beta for extra torque, a modest single-name short to offset gross exposure, and cash held for weekly rebalancing flexibility.

positions.thesis: Core AI compute bottleneck; Blackwell/next-gen ramp keeps NVDA the highest-quality way to own the capex cycle.
Azure AI monetization plus enterprise Copilot adoption gives durable, lower-volatility AI platform exposure; increased weight to replace decaying leveraged-semis beta with a steadier AI-capex proxy.
Custom silicon/networking for hyperscaler AI clusters diversifies compute exposure beyond GPUs.
MI-series datacenter GPU share gains and cyclical semis exposure at a more reasonable multiple than NVDA.
HBM/memory remains structurally tight for AI servers despite the recent pullback.
Relative laggard in on-device/enterprise AI monetization versus platform peers; funds long book while staying within short-side limits.

reassessment_note: Week 2 Info Desk (2026-07-25, drip protocol — released items only): The only new information this week (Info items 1-2) is price action confirming the 3x-leveraged SOXL sleeve is behaving exactly as leveraged-ETF theory predicts in a choppy tape: it rallied mid-week then round-tripped back to the same $136.81 close with a violent -13.14% single-day drop on 7/24, still down >40% for the month even as the underlying SMH is down a much milder ~9%. That gap is pure volatility-decay drag from daily resetting, not a semis-thesis break. Rather than hold a leveraged position bleeding value on whipsaw action, I'm exiting the SOXL sleeve entirely and redeploying into MSFT (lower-beta, still core AI platform exposure) and cash, while leaving the unleveraged core (NVDA/AVGO/AMD/MU) and the AAPL funding short untouched to keep turnover -- and costs -- minimal. Adding stops on the semis-linked names given the now-demonstrated intraday volatility.
